deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. This page continues the previous one: meridian-circle observations of fundamental stars at the Göttingen observatory in April–May, used to fix the latitude (polar height, about 51°32'). The observations are reduced to mean places for 1819.0.

Dating (my inference). The lunar-node argument on this page is 39°18' on Apr 20. That is the value of Ω for 1818.30 (Ω ≈ 125.04° + 19.3413°·181.7 yr ≡ 39.3°). The precession columns also vanish at the following 1 January. So the observations are from April–May 1818, reduced to 1819.0. 'Pr. b. 1819' on the previous page means precession to the beginning of 1819.

CONVENTION. Each table row reduces an apparent place to the mean place of 1819.0. The columns are: aberration | lunar nutation | solar nutation | precession plus proper motion | sum. The previous page shows the sum being subtracted from the apparent declination (Procyon: 5°40'56.79 − 10.56 = 5°40'46.23).

(1) POLLUX DECLINATION. A five-line table (Apr 20 – May 30, every 10 days) of the four terms and their sum, for example Apr 20: 2.83 + 8.67 + 0.38 + 5.66 = 17.54. The precession column falls by about 0.22" per 10 days, i.e. about −8.0"/yr. This matches 20.05"·cos α for α ≈ 113.5° (Pollux).

(2) SIRIUS DECLINATION: the coefficients, computed in Gaussian form A·sin(argument + B).

(a) Aberration, Δ = A·sin(⊙ + 85°54'), log A = 1.1129.
- ⊙ is the Sun's longitude: 29°57', 39°38', 49°17', 58°53', 68°27'. Its 10-day steps of about 9°40' shrink toward aphelion.
- The logs 9.9542, 9.9105, 9.8481, 9.7609, 9.6364 are log sin(⊙ + 85°54').
- The products are 11.67, 10.55, 9.14, 7.48, 5.61.
- Check from theory (mine): with k = 20.25", α = 99.28°, δ = −16.47°:
  Δδ = −k[cos⊙·cosε(tanε cosδ − sinα sinδ) + sin⊙·cosα sinδ] ≈ −12.94 cos⊙ − 0.92 sin⊙.
  Hence A = 12.97 (log 1.1129) and B = 265°56' = 180° + 85°56'. Gauss's columns therefore carry reversed sign; see 'muta signa' below.

(b) Lunar nutation, Δ = 9.59·sin(Ω + 263°4'), log = 0.9819.
- Ω = 39°18', 38°14', 37°11' (Apr 20, May 10, May 30). It falls by about 32' per 10 days.
- The logs 9.9267n, 9.9317n, 9.9364n are log sin(Ω + 263°4').
- The values are −8.11 … −8.29. The 10-day intermediate values are interpolated.
- Decomposing (mine): A·sin(Ω + 83°4') with A = 9.59 corresponds to Δε-amplitude N ≈ 9.65" and Δψ-amplitude P ≈ 18.0", applied in Δδ = Δε sinα + Δψ sinε cosα. Again the sign is reversed.

(c) Solar nutation, Δ = 0.49·sin(2⊙ + 262°), log = 9.690.
- 2⊙ = 59°54', 79°16', 98°34', 117°46', 136°54'.
- The logs are 9.790n, 9.506n, 7.995, 9.529, 9.798.
- The values are −0.30, −0.16, +0.00, +0.17, +0.31.

(d) Precession plus proper motion.
- Annual rate: 1.11 (proper motion) + 3.24 (precession, = 20.05·|cos α|) = 4.35"/yr.
- In logs (margin column): log 4.35 = 0.63849, log 365.25 = 2.56259, daily rate log = 8.07590.
- Days remaining to year end: 365 − 110.2 = 254.8 (log 2.40620) for Apr 20, and 365 − 150.1 = 214.9 (log 2.33224) for May 30. The numbers 110.2 and 150.1 are day-of-year counts.
- Value = −4.35·(days remaining)/365.25: −3.03 for Apr 20 (written −3.02) and −2.56 for May 30.

(e) Sums: +0.23, −0.68, −1.86, −3.27, −4.93. The note reads 'muta signa propter decl. austr.' (change signs because the declination is southern).

(f) Sirius mean declination.
- −16°28'9.90" − 17.36" = −16°28'27.26" (1819).
- My interpretation: 17.36 = 4 × 4.34"/yr. This would bring a catalogue declination for 1815 (probably Bessel's 1815 fundamental stars) forward to 1819.

(3) LATITUDE FROM SIRIUS.
- Corrected zenith distances plus refraction:
  - 67°58'34.43 + 2'18.31 = 68°0'52.74
  - 67°58'34.07 + 2'19.04 = 68°0'53.11
  - 67°58'22.27 + 2'17.40 = 68°0'39.67
  - 67°58'23.42 + 2'17.12 = 68°0'40.54
- Adding the sign-changed reduction gives the mean zenith distance for 1819. The reductions +0.28, +0.38, +0.79, +1.33 are interpolated with second differences from the sums: Apr 26 → −0.284, Apr 27 → −0.379, May 1 → −0.786, May 6 → about −1.36.
  - 68°0'53.02, 53.49, 40.46, 41.87.
- Latitude φ = z + δ = z − 16°28'27.26:
  - 51°32'25.76, 26.23, 13.20, 14.61.
- The 12–13" jump between Apr 27 and May 1 shows an instrumental disturbance.

(4) LEVEL / INDEX, May 1 early ('früh').
- Two readings in each of three columns are averaged pairwise:
  - (24.1 + 18.5)/2 = 21.3
  - (33.5 + 28.45)/2 = 30.975
  - (15.3 + 10.85)/2 = 13.075
- The adopted value is 3'20.89. This quantity, about 3'21", is the index/level correction subtracted from the circle readings; compare 45°53'46.25 → 45°50'24.31 on the previous page.
- Note: 'Nachmittag stark an das Fernrohr gestossen' — in the afternoon the telescope was struck hard. The next page reports re-levelling (adopted result 3'22"2).

(5) NEW TRANSITS AND ZENITH DISTANCES.
- Capella: wires 5h2'50.3, 5h3'13.6, 5h3'37.1. The mean is 5h3'13.67, used on the next page with clock correction −0.49. The circle reading is 5°47'14.7, followed by the pair 2'25.8 (2'27.0 struck) and 2'7.6.
- Rigel: 59°59'15.5, marked '::' as doubtful.
- '[ε/β] Tauri': 23°8'25.4, with the pair 3'36.3 / 3'19.5.
- Checks (mine), subtracting about 3'21" index and adding refraction:
  - Capella → δ ≈ 45°48'.
  - Rigel → δ ≈ −8°25'.
  - the Tauri star → δ ≈ +28°27'. This fits β Tauri for 1819 but not ε Tauri (δ ≈ +18°49', z would be about 32°43').
- Bottom line: barometer 27 Zoll 7.2 Linien, thermometer +13.7° (Réaumur), for the refraction.
errors: Sirius precession Apr 20: 4.35·254.8/365.25 = 3.035, so −3.03 or −3.04; written −3.02. The step to Apr 30 (−2.92) is then 0.10 instead of the uniform 0.119. The Apr 20 sum would be +0.22 instead of +0.23. Minor slip.
Lunar nutation Apr 20: log 0.9819 + 9.9267 gives 8.104, i.e. 8.10; written −8.11. Rounding or unrounded inputs, 0.01".
Interpolated reduction for May 6: second-difference interpolation gives about −1.36; Gauss uses 1.33. A 0.03" difference, possibly due to the exact time.
Level mean: the simple mean of 3'21.3, 3'30.975 and 3'13.075 is 3'21.78, but 3'20.89 is adopted. The rule used is not evident; same pattern on the next page (simple mean 3'23.1, result 3'22.2).
Mixed year lengths in the precession: 365 − 110.2 in the numerator but 365.25 in the denominator. Negligible.
The latitudes 51°32'13"–26" differ from the true 51°31'48" by about 25–38". This reflects the uncorrected index/level state and catalogue declinations, not an arithmetic error.

results.what: Reduction of apparent to mean declination (aberration, lunar and solar nutation, precession plus proper motion) for Pollux and Sirius, with each periodic term written as A·sin(argument + B) and evaluated by logarithms
results.modern_name: Apparent-place reduction via star constants (Besselian-day-number type)
results.usually_credited_to: Bradley (aberration, nutation), Lagrange/Laplace/Gauss (Gaussian sine forms), Bessel (Tabulae Regiomontanae, 1830, day numbers)

results.what: Latitude of Göttingen from meridian zenith distances of Sirius, phi = z + delta, with refraction and index (level) correction
results.modern_name: Latitude determination by meridian zenith distances of fundamental stars
results.usually_credited_to: standard practice; Gauss's Göttingen latitude work c. 1818–1820 is documented

results.what: Interpolation of tabulated 10-day reductions to observation dates using second differences

deep.surprise_reason: Routine observatory reductions and latitude determination from Gauss's early Göttingen meridian work (1818). The numbers are internally consistent and of documentary interest only.
